# ASP.NET Core security

- Use dedicated input/output models with validation and explicit mapping. Do not expose EF entities or accept over-posted ownership, role, tenant, and administrative fields.
- Apply authentication and authorization before endpoint execution. Use policy/resource-based handlers for object-level checks and define a deliberate fallback policy rather than relying on route conventions.
- Keep middleware order secure: forwarded headers from known proxies, exception handling/HSTS, HTTPS redirection, routing, CORS, authentication, authorization, antiforgery as applicable, then endpoints.
- Preserve Razor encoding and Tag Helpers. Avoid `Html.Raw` and JavaScript/URL interpolation of untrusted data.
- For cookie authentication, use secure cookie settings, antiforgery on unsafe methods, session/token rotation, and server-side invalidation where required. Do not disable antiforgery globally for mixed browser/API apps.
- Configure CORS with named policies and exact origins; do not combine credentials with wildcard/reflected origins.
- Protect Data Protection keys outside source and persist/share them safely for multi-instance services. Separate environments and applications with appropriate discriminators.
- Keep Developer Exception Page, detailed identity errors, Swagger/management endpoints, and sensitive health details out of untrusted production access.
- Set Kestrel/form/multipart/request limits and downstream timeouts. Validate proxy headers and HTTPS scheme only from trusted network hops.
- Keep secrets out of `appsettings*.json` committed values and user-secrets in production; use approved configuration/secret providers.
